scope: Independent retail-client body evidence for the 39 legacy semantic dependency rows consumed by this catalog.
rule: Address, opcode, size, symbol, or dispatch-edge agreement alone is a cross-check. A closed row requires a body observation that supports the retained label or a narrower replacement label.

rows.supportedLabel: 0x00c9 chat-message sender with a u32 selector and a 0x200-byte text field
rows.observation: The sender writes opcode 0x00c9 and body size 0x218, writes its u32 selector argument at application offset 0, zero-fills the 0x200-byte field at application offset 4 before copying the source text into it, and enqueues through FUN_00DB3E30; these field writes independently establish a selector-tagged chat message, while captures confirm a 552-byte subpacket and 536-byte application body.

rows.supportedLabel: PartyMapMarkerUpdatePacket client route with sixteen reserved 0x28-byte rows and a count byte at application offset 0x290
rows.tool: XIVLegacy Ghidra DumpFunctionDecomp.java, build_data_dependency_catalog.py, and capture payload analysis
rows.observation: The central dispatcher routes opcode 0x018d through FUN_00575550, which gates on owner offset 0x4d8 and forwards the application data to FUN_0055CF70. That apply function copies three header dwords, sign-extends the u8 count at application offset 0x290, and transposes count 0x28-byte source rows into 0x78-byte client rows. The wire layout reserves sixteen source rows, but retail contains no compare or clamp to 16. All 60 retained subpackets are 696-byte subpackets; count is 1 in 58 samples and 2 in 2 samples, so observed max=2. This establishes the client-side party map-marker update route and layout, not a server implementation declaration or behavior.

rows.supportedLabel: SetSpecialEventWorkPacket client state update with a 24-byte application payload
rows.tool: XIVLegacy Ghidra DumpFunctionDecomp.java, client Lua API cross-reference, and capture payload analysis
rows.observation: FUN_00576050 expands application byte +1 into eight flags, reads eight u16 values at +2 through +0x10, writes the first u16 to owner +0x38, and forwards all sixteen values to FUN_0075D2D0. That helper writes the flags at target +0x84..+0x8b and the u16 values at +0x8c..+0x9a; WorldMaster _getSpecialEventWork reads the same arrays through FUN_0075D390 and FUN_0075D3A0. All 11 retained subpackets are 56 bytes across 8 captures, while the aggregate corpus count is 12. Their 24-byte application payloads have zero flags, eventWork6=1, every other retained event-work value zero, and a zero six-byte tail. This proves the client SetSpecialEventWork operation and field layout, not a source-owned server enum declaration or server behavior.

rows.supportedLabel: Single string-bearing entry factory and queue insertion
rows.observation: The thunk reaches FUN_006CC390 through FUN_006CD790. The body reads u32 values at payload offsets 8 and 0x0c, consumes string objects at offsets 0x10 and 0x20, allocates one 0x40-byte entry builder, and calls FUN_006CBFB0. That factory installs the observed entry-builder vtable, allocates one 0xf8-byte child object, stores it at builder offset 0x38, clears the byte at 0x3c, replaces the prior entry through FUN_006C4330, and enqueues the new pointer through FUN_007238B0. A zero value at payload offset 0x0c selects the sentinel-id branch; there is no record loop or drop gate.

rows.supportedLabel: 0x018a client manager-row copy and commit route with a 120-byte application payload
rows.tool: XIVLegacy Ghidra DumpFunctionDecomp.java and corpus aggregate audit
rows.observation: FUN_00576380 forwards the application payload through FUN_006C82A0 to FUN_006C6A70. The helper uses the signed low byte at application offset 0x60 as its loop bound, copies one u32 from +0x40+4*i and one eight-byte pair from +8*i into each manager row, then commits through unresolved FUN_006C58C0. Static client evidence gives a 120-byte application payload with the copied arrays at +0 and +0x40 and an unread 20-byte tail at +0x64..+0x77. The corpus reports one aggregate event but retains no payload samples or layout, so observedIn and payloadLengths remain empty. This proves a client manager-row copy/commit route, not the imported SetActiveLinkshell packet noun, exact row domain, a server implementation declaration, or server behavior.

rows.supportedLabel: 0x0193 multiplexed client state/config dispatcher with an 8-byte application payload
rows.tool: XIVLegacy Ghidra DumpFunctionDecomp.java and capture payload analysis
rows.observation: The central dispatcher passes packet fields +0x10, +0x14, and +0x08 to FUN_00578C90. That handler switches on the first application u32: values below 0x10 enter the indexed FUN_0075F3E0 worker; 0x10 through 0x12 and 0x16 write direct state slots; 0x13 enters a string/config path; 0x14 performs a one-time init gate; and 0x15 enters unresolved FUN_00576020. All 9 retained subpackets are 40 bytes across 8 captures, matching the 9 aggregate events. The retained subopcode distribution is 0x14 in 8 samples and 0x12 in 1 sample; this proves a multiplexed client state/config route but not the imported SetControlState packet noun, exact low-range/string/0x15 semantics, a server implementation declaration, or server behavior.

rows.supportedLabel: 0x012f client work-state update route with one leading dword, 32 copied bytes, and an unresolved four-byte tail
rows.tool: XIVLegacy Ghidra FindOpcodeImmediate.java, DumpFunctionDecomp.java, and analyze_payload_layouts.py
rows.observation: The builder writes opcode 0x012f and record size 0x38, copies a caller-supplied leading dword plus a 32-byte zero-initialized staging area populated by a runtime-length generic range copy, and calls FUN_004D6D30. CharaBase and DirectorBase _updateWork implementations reach the builder through FUN_00767FC0 and FUN_00767C00. The wire forwarder performs a 0x28-byte copy from record+0x18, including an unwritten four-byte stack tail at record+0x3c after the leading dword and four qwords. All 44 captures are 72-byte subpackets and retain a nonconstant tail. This supports a client work-state update route, but not a specific server packet noun.

rows.supportedLabel: _getAchievementRate client request carrying one achievement-id lookup key
rows.observation: The builder writes opcode 0x0135 and body size 0x18, copies its one u32 payload value to application offset 0, and calls FUN_004D6D30. Its sole caller FUN_00705EB0 is MyPlayer vtable slot 112 and the registered _getAchievementRate implementation. On the valid path FUN_005819A0 returns the first runtime argument-vector entry +0x8 value, which FUN_00705EB0 forwards unchanged to the builder. Independent retail achievement receive evidence identifies the corresponding lookup domain as achievementId. The exact server method noun is not embedded in the client.

rows.supportedLabel: EventStartPacket generic command-event envelope
rows.tool: XIVLegacy retail asm, preserved-script metadata, and capture payload analysis
rows.observation: FUN_00776760 writes opcode 0x012d and record size 0xc8, stages four u32 values, one u8, 32 inline bytes, and a 128-byte event tail, then sends through FUN_004D6D30, FUN_004E0240, and FUN_00DAE010. The preserved PlayerBase command path reaches this builder through _callServerOnCommand and FUN_006EE680/FUN_0075E3A0. Captures contain 126 total 216-byte subpackets, including combat and noncombat scenarios. No stable scalar gameCommand row id, range constant, resource check, or server-side CanUse rule is established; command-specific eligibility remains behind command.canFire and native dynamic dispatch.

rows.supportedLabel: 0x01cb client no-op callback route with no supported clientbound packet noun
rows.tool: XIVLegacy Ghidra dispatcher, vtable-slot, and function-body analysis
rows.observation: The zone dispatch map routes opcode 0x01cb to callback slot 173, and the retail ZoneProtoDown callback table resolves that slot to FUN_00DB8FA0. The function body immediately returns with RET 0xc and reads no packet fields or client state. A separate client-to-server builder FUN_004CA100 emits the same opcode integer through the zone send path, but that opposite-direction use does not establish a clientbound packet noun or behavior.

rows.supportedLabel: 0x00ce dual-builder client operation with a 0x38-byte record and unresolved semantics
rows.tool: XIVLegacy Ghidra packet-builder and capture payload analysis
rows.observation: FUN_00763DC0 and FUN_0076D610 each write opcode 0x00ce and record size 0x38 into a stack-built packet before calling FUN_004D6D10. The shared zone path continues through FUN_004E0240 and FUN_00DAE010. Both retained captures are 72-byte subpackets in cutscene_book.pcapng, comprising the 16-byte subpacket header plus the 56-byte builder record; their 40-byte application payload does not establish a stable operation noun.
